scope: Agent review of actual final-build native VRAM captures, supported by separate keyboard, focus, pixel, ownership and persisted-byte tasks. Not a participant usability study or external screen-reader qualification.
findings: Clarity: independent accessibility checkmarks and saved-state messages distinguish immediate accessibility saves from Appearance preview/Apply.
Convenience: actual keyboard-only installation, Start search, Files navigation and F6 panes keep ordinary tasks available without a mouse; F1/Escape retains work.
User friendliness: Focus Help uses the actual current control name and role, including the picker own focus, checkboxes and Dismiss; existing file reviews retain ownership.
Graphical quality: shared native Inter typography, measured labels, bounded layouts and explicit Focus Help/first-guide boundaries remain clear in compact Light/Dark and physical 4K high contrast.

Readability: reviewed essential controls/text have no overlap or clipping within their active surface; overlaid help intentionally covers inactive underlying controls. Light and Dark first-start cards now have visible contrasting edges.
Physical and logical pointer positions and actual rendered rectangles agree at 150%/200%, including clipped screen edges; pixel observations are separate from a capture-timing assumption.

In high-contrast reduced-effects mode, picker and notification text/actions remain legible, but their black outer surfaces do not have the explicit outline used by Focus Help. Retain this visual polish observation for the M12.18 final review.
retained_observations: M12.18 final controller/original-app and site-sharing observations
